title: Rollouts: persist activity timeline + emit audit log events for rollout actions
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: Console: Rollout details now show an Activity timeline (start/step/pause/approval/rollback) and all rollout actions emit customer-auditable events (actor, route, rollout_id, before/after).
description:
Context
We need a GA-grade, customer-visible timeline of what happened during a Hosted canary rollout, and we need security-grade audit log coverage for the same set of actions. Today we have some internal orchestrator events, but they are (a) not normalized for Console display and (b) not emitted to the audit pipeline consistently.

This PR adds:
1) A persisted rollout activity timeline (customer visible) stored alongside rollout state.
2) Audit log emission for rollout actions with consistent payloads + diffing.

Scope
- Rollout actions covered: create, start, pause, resume, step_change (traffic percentage), approve (where approval gate is enabled), rollback, auto_pause/auto_rollback (stop-condition driven), and config edits that affect the rollout plan.
- Activity timeline is stored as an append-only log with a small canonical schema and rendered by Console (DES-755).
- Audit log events follow the Security spec (see "Audit schema" section below) and include actor identity + request id + tenant id.

Implementation notes
- Activity timeline
  - New table: rollout_activity_events (partitioned by tenant_id, indexed by rollout_id, created_at).
  - Events are written by rollout-orchestrator on successful state transitions only.
  - Events are also written for "attempted but denied" actions *only* to the audit pipeline (not the customer timeline), to avoid confusing customers and to prevent info leaks about policy internals.
  - Console reads from /v1/rollouts/{id}/activity (paginated) and displays a merged list (human-readable + machine metadata).

- Audit log events
  - New event type family: rollout.*
  - Emission point is the Console backend rollout orchestration service (server-side), not the client, to guarantee actor attribution and to ensure events exist for API callers.
  - Every event includes: actor (user/service), tenant_id, rollout_id, route_id, baseline_model_ref, canary_model_ref, state_before, state_after, change_summary, request_id, ip (if user), user_agent (if user), and policy_decision_id (when a policy check is involved).
  - For step changes, we include before/after traffic split and step index.
  - For approvals, we include gate name and required role.

Audit schema (high level)
- event_name examples:
  - rollout.created
  - rollout.started
  - rollout.step_changed
  - rollout.paused
  - rollout.resumed
  - rollout.approved
  - rollout.rolled_back
  - rollout.auto_paused
  - rollout.auto_rolled_back
- change_summary is intentionally compact (string) and not a nested object to keep SIEM exports consistent across sinks.

Cardinality / PII
- We do not include prompt text, completions, request bodies, or model outputs.
- Model refs are version identifiers already present in route config (e.g., "llama-3.1-70b:2025-03-01").
- User identity fields follow the existing audit pipeline normalization.

Testing
- Unit tests: timeline serialization, audit event payload validation (required fields), state transition mapping.
- Integration tests: orchestrator action -> timeline record inserted -> audit event emitted.
- Manual: exercised via Console wizard in staging; validated timeline ordering and audit event presence in audit-events-dev index.

Rollout / ops
- Feature-flagged behind hosted_canary_rollouts_activity_timeline (default off).
- Safe to deploy independently: timeline storage is additive; audit events are additive.
- Backfill: none for GA; existing beta rollouts will show activity from the moment the flag is enabled.

Notes / follow-ups
- We should align wording of change_summary with the copy in Console (DES-755) in a follow-up to avoid drift.
- We currently write activity on successful transitions; if we want visibility into repeated failures (e.g., retry storms), that belongs in telemetry not the customer timeline.

Screenshots
- Added in comments: Rollout details > Activity tab with start/step/pause/approve/rollback entries.

Checklist
- [x] Audit pipeline events emitted for all supported actions
- [x] Actor attribution correct for both Console UI and API callers
- [x] Activity timeline is append-only and paginated
- [x] No PII beyond existing audit standards
- [x] Docs note added to internal audit event catalog (separate PR)

Refs
- Linear: ENG-9171
- Design: DES-755
- GA driver: PM-1843

conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Can we guarantee we emit audit events for API callers (not only Console UI) and that the payloads never include request bodies? Also please include policy_decision_id when available for governance tracing.

Michael Nguyen (Author): Yes—emission is in console-backend server handlers shared by UI + API. No request bodies are logged; only identifiers + before/after state. Added policy_decision_id plumbed from policy engine response and a unit test that asserts request_body is not referenced.
Chloe Martin (Console backend): Endpoint needs pagination and stable ordering; Console will poll. Also make sure we don’t block rollout progression on audit sink latency.

Michael Nguyen (Author): Added cursor-based pagination ordered by created_at + id. Audit emission is fire-and-forget via existing buffered publisher; failures are logged and surfaced to SRE metrics but do not fail the user action (matches existing audit behavior).
Felix Schneider (Metrics/UI): For the customer timeline, include a concise string we can display without re-deriving from state diffs. But keep machine fields for tooltips.

Michael Nguyen (Author): Added display_message generated at write time (English string) plus structured columns (action, from_state, to_state, step_percent_before/after, actor_type). Console can choose either, but default is display_message.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth): Please verify actor attribution for service accounts when a rollout is advanced via API token; also include actor_id even if email is null.
Michael Nguyen (Author): Fixed actor mapping to prefer principal_id always; email is optional. Added integration test for service-account advancement.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): If audit publisher is down, we need a metric and a runbook pointer; also activity table growth—what’s retention?

Michael Nguyen (Author): Added metric audit_publish_failures_total{event_family=rollout}. Retention: activity timeline follows rollout retention policy (90d default) enforced by existing cleanup job; added index + partitioning to keep scans bounded.
notes_for_release_manager: Requires db migration 20250314_add_rollout_activity_events.sql. Feature-flag hosted_canary_rollouts_activity_timeline remains OFF by default; enable per-tenant during beta/GA enablement. No backfill.
